fuel_cost.reason: Range follows gas. Gas is 62% of capacity and 54% of 2025 output (112.7 of 207.2 TWh, 10-K segment tables), and Henry Hub annual averages moved about -15% to +50% a year in 2023-26 (EIA). Gas at ~60% of fuel cost x a ~+-30% gas move = ~+-18% a year: FY27 +-12%, FY28 +-18%, FY29 +-20%. The gas price also moves the power price, and the row now moves both together. The 98%/78% hedge figures cover power sold (10-K Item 7A: gas hedges are used as a proxy for power-price exposure, and fuel is bought spot and near term, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1692819/000169281926000006/vistra-20251231.htm). So on the hedged slice, realized power price stays fixed and the fuel move is a pure margin squeeze. On the unhedged slice (FY26 0%, FY27 2%, FY28 22%, FY29 ~50% as in gen_price), power price moves with gas: each $1/MWh of fleet fuel change moves the unhedged power price by $1.11/MWh (= 0.60 gas share of fuel / 0.54 gas share of output, i.e. the price-setting gas unit passes its fuel cost through at Vistra's own gas-fleet heat rate). That pass-through is a convention, not a disclosed number; a higher market heat rate would pass through more and narrow the range further. Outside (11-10, MarketScreener roundup 2026-10-27): Henry Hub 2027 EIA $3.16, NYMEX strip $3.13, BofA $4.00, Enverus $3.25 vs 2026 $3.48; 2028-30 strip ~$3.65-3.70. Converted to fuel $/MWh as 25.97 x (1 + 0.6 x gas change), holding non-gas fuel flat: FY27 24.5-28.3, FY28 ~26.9. Note: the model's FY28 fuel (28.93, +11%) sits above the strip-implied ~26.9; worth a look at the next VST update.

aws_turn.reason: Filed: AWS revenue $90.8B 2023, $107.6B 2024, $128.7B 2025, 9M 2026 $125.8B; AWS net PP&E $72.7B / $110.7B / $190.1B at YE2023-25 (segment note XBRL: 10-K FY2025 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000004/amzn-20251231.htm; Q3 2026 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000040/amzn-20260930.htm). Low = the filed ~-26% decline runs one more year (FY27 x0.86), then the model's path; high = +-10%/yr x sqrt(years ahead) (capacity monetizing faster). Was +-10% from our scenario cases.
